criteria.criterion: docs/spec.toml entry OLY-B-SET-02 has a mechanism other than "none" naming the roster code path and test, owner Athena, and a measure ending with `status: not shown` and the test command.
criteria.evidence: From the diff: the mechanism names `ROSTER`/`roster_entry` in crates/athena-core/src/jev.rs and the test crates/athena-core/tests/model_roster.rs. Owner is "Athena". The measure is "Run `cargo test -p athena-core --test model_roster`; ... No `athena status` line shows the roster; status: not shown". The xtask spec test passed 30/30, including the_real_spec_passes and every_active_requirement_has_a_mechanism_an_owner_and_a_measure.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core` (the new roster test): it asserts the roster holds Opus, Sonnet and Haiku model names and Jev with the ai-gateway.vercel.sh endpoint; it fails when the roster entry for any of the four is removed and passes with the change.
criteria.evidence: roster_holds_opus_sonnet_haiku_and_jev passed (1 passed). The test looks up opus, sonnet and haiku through roster_entry and checks each model starts with `claude-` and contains its family name. It checks Jev's model == MODEL and endpoint == Some(ENDPOINT), that ENDPOINT contains ai-gateway.vercel.sh, and that ROSTER.len() == 4. I could not mutate the files because the verifier role changes nothing, so the fail-without check is reasoned, not run: the test does not compile without ROSTER/roster_entry. Removing an entry either breaks the `[RosterEntry; 4]` type or, once resized, makes roster_entry return None (panic) and fails the len assertion.

criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks for ab9185fc show fmt, clippy and test passing (CI run 43141115910). I ran `cargo test -p xtask --test spec` myself: 30 passed, 0 failed.

findings.summary: Soundness: the roster is a hard-coded list that nothing reads, and its test only checks that constants exist. It does not show that work uses Opus, Sonnet and Haiku.
findings.evidence: A grep for ROSTER/roster_entry/RosterEntry finds only jev.rs, the new test, spec.toml and CHANGELOG.md. No code path uses it. The models work actually runs with come from athena.toml [models] (reader/producer_default = claude-sonnet-5-5, producer_allowed includes claude-haiku-5-5, verifier = claude-opus-5-5), loaded by crates/athena-data/src/config.rs. ROSTER copies those strings by hand. If athena.toml dropped Haiku or moved to a new model version, this test would still pass and ROSTER would silently go stale. That breaks the behavior-evidence default ("check the requested behavior happening, not that types, files or wiring exist"). It also departs from the accepted reading's "Opus, Sonnet, Haiku via configured roles". Simpler, more correct alternative: check the configured roles. For example, a test or config validation that loads the repository's athena.toml through athena-data's config loader and asserts its [models] roles cover an Opus, a Sonnet and a Haiku model, alongside the existing Jev ENDPOINT/MODEL check. Putting the Claude model list inside the Jev client module is also an odd home.

findings.evidence: No change was needed: the jev module is already public, and the integration test compiles and imports athena_core::jev::ROSTER.

summary: The change adds a hard-coded `ROSTER` to jev.rs (Opus, Sonnet and Haiku model names, plus Jev reusing MODEL and ENDPOINT), adds a test that checks it, and fills in OLY-B-SET-02's mechanism, owner and measure (`status: not shown`). The new test passes. The xtask spec test passes (30/30). The recorded fmt, clippy and test checks passed. All four acceptance criteria are met. The verdict is still fail, on a major soundness finding: no code reads ROSTER. It is a hand copy of the model names that athena.toml [models] actually configures, so the test proves only that constants exist, not that work uses Opus, Sonnet and Haiku. Dropping Haiku from the config or moving to a new model version would leave the test green. The fix is to check the configured roles: load athena.toml through athena-data's config and assert the roles cover all three Claude families, next to the existing Jev constant check. Minor: xtask/shard-timings.txt changed outside the deliverables list, though the repository requires that line for a new test file. I did not run the remove-an-entry mutation, because the verifier may not edit files; the fail-without result is reasoned from the code.
